source.authors: Giacinto S. Germinara, Marco Pistillo, Raffaele Griffo, Antonio P. Garonna, Antonella Di Palma
source.title: Electroantennographic Responses of Aromia bungii (Faldermann, 1835) (Coleoptera, Cerambycidae) to a Range of Volatile Compounds

value: male and female antennae gave similar EAG responses to 90 volatile compounds; 17 compounds differed significantly between sexes
method: electroantennography on antennae of males and females, 90 volatile compounds, 1 mg load (10 uL of 100 ug/uL mineral oil solution) per stimulus, mineral oil control and (Z)-3-hexenol standard (10 uL of 10 ug/uL) presented at the start and after each group of five test compounds
conditions: larvae in logs collected from infested apricot trees near Marigliano (Naples, Italy) and reared to adults; 10 to 15 day old unmated adults; each compound tested on five antennae of different insects of each sex, total number of insects not stated; stimuli in random sequence, 1 min apart; a second set used a (Z)-3-hexenol dose series of 0.001 to 100 ug/uL in ascending order on flagellomeres seven to nine; Results: all compounds elicited measurable EAG responses in both sexes (p < 0.05, Wilcoxon rank sum tests), from 0.028 +/- 0.003 mV ((E,E)-2,4-hexadienal) to 1.197 +/- 0.067 mV ((E)-2-hexenol) in males and from 0.019 +/- 0.001 mV (ethyl acetate) to 0.979 +/- 0.057 mV ((E)-2-hexenol) in females; of the 17 differing compounds, male responses exceeded female for 12 and female exceeded male for 5; stimulus amounts are nominal loads, not measured air concentrations
quote: A large degree of similarity between the EAG responses of males and females was observed with only 17 of the 90 compounds tested eliciting significant differences.
note: Sentence copied whole from the MDPI page (sentence returned by the page tool in two consecutive segments). Licence: page metadata gives CC BY 3.0, Crossref gives CC BY 4.0 for the version of record. DOI, volume, issue and author order verified on Crossref. Species absent from main for sense_chemical (git grep of whole docs tree; only the d217 progress note names the paper as held).

source.authors: Qi Sun, Weicheng Yang, Sheng Liang, Mengqing Zhou, Fen Liu, Xianyu Li, Bibo Zhou, Tianyu Liang
source.title: Electrophysiological and Behavioral Responses of Phthonoloba viridifasciata (Lepidoptera: Geometridae) to Volatiles from Alsophila spinulosa

value: female EAG 0.387 +/- 0.027 mV to 4-ethylbenzaldehyde (largest of the five compounds) and 0.206 +/- 0.008 mV to decane (smallest)
method: electroantennography of adults, five host-fern volatiles in n-hexane, 10 uL on filter paper (10 x 30 mm strip), 0.5 s stimulus, 30 s between stimuli, n-hexane first and last
conditions: larvae collected at the Alsophila National Nature Reserve, Chishui, Guizhou, China and reared separately by sex; adults 2 to 3 days old, unmated; five concentrations (1e-1 to 1e-5 mol/L) applied in ascending order, one stimulation each; the quoted sentence does not say which concentration the mV values come from and the number of antennae is not stated; all five compounds gave EAG responses in both sexes; females were significantly above males for undecane (p < 0.05) and 4-ethylbenzaldehyde (p < 0.01), with no significant sex difference for decane, p-ethylacetophenone and m-ethylacetophenone; stimuli are nominal solution amounts, not measured air concentrations
quote: Female adults exhibited stronger EAG responses to 4-ethylbenzaldehyde (EAG = 0.387 ± 0.027 mV) among all tested compounds, while showing the weakest EAG response to decane (EAG = 0.206 ± 0.008 mV).
note: Sentence copied whole from the MDPI page (returned in two consecutive segments). Licence: page metadata CC BY 3.0, Crossref CC BY 4.0 vor. DOI, volume, issue and author order verified on Crossref. Species absent from whole docs tree except the d217 note listing the paper as unopened.

source.authors: Mengqing Zhou, Weicheng Yang, Gaoyin Wu, Xiaona Zhang, Fen Liu, Qi Sun, Xianyu Li, Jiya Wu, Tianyu Liang, Bibo Zhou
source.title: Antennal Responses and Odorant-Binding Protein 7 Binding of Rhoptroceros cyatheae (Selandriidae: Rhopographus) to Volatile Organic Compounds from Alsophila spinulosa

value: males gave stronger EAG responses than females to most of nine host-fern volatiles tested
method: electroantennography of adult sawflies, nine commercially available host volatiles in n-hexane at 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10 and 100 uL/mL, 10 uL on a filter paper strip, n-hexane control first, concentrations from low to high with each applied once
conditions: adults and larvae field-collected in the Guizhou Chishui Alsophila National Nature Reserve, adults collected 1 to 3 days after emergence and reared separately to keep them virgin; 27 females and 27 males, each sample tested in triplicate; the nine tested compounds are a subset of 13 EAG-active GC-EAD compounds (the rest lacked pure commercial standards or were unstable); the Abstract says nine volatiles were identified as eliciting responses while Results section 2.1 says 13; sex differences were concentration-dependent and larger at high concentrations; 3-methylheptane gave slightly higher EAG in females but weak overall, and 3-methylheptane, tridecane, tetradecane and cedrene gave only weak responses in both sexes; antenna preparation not described; stimuli are nominal solution amounts
quote: For most volatile compounds, male sawflies exhibited stronger responses than females.
note: Sentence copied whole from the MDPI page. Licence: page metadata CC BY 3.0, Crossref CC BY 4.0 vor. DOI, volume, issue and author order verified on Crossref. Species and DOI absent from main (held lead from d217, p-xylene sentence now within the word limit but not needed). Name as printed in the title.

source.authors: Hua Xie, Hui Yuan, Yuyun Wang, Xinyu Tang, Meiru Yang, Li Zheng, Zongbo Li
source.title: Compound Eye Structure and Phototactic Dimorphism in the Yunnan Pine Shoot Beetle, Tomicus yunnanensis (Coleoptera: Scolytinae)

value: phototaxis peaks: females at 360, 380 and 700 nm; males at 360 and 400 nm
method: three-chamber phototaxis apparatus with monochromator light from 300 to 700 nm in 20 nm steps, 10 min dark adaptation then 10 min exposure, beetles counted in each zone
conditions: adults collected alive from pine shoots in January to February at JiuLong Shan Forestry Station, Yunnan; rearing and exact age not described ('newly emerged'); 30 same-sex adults per wavelength trial, three replicates, each beetle used once, per-sex numbers ambiguous; light intensity set by calibrating irradiance to 300 lux at the stationary zone, a photometric unit that is not photon-matched across wavelengths and not checked per wavelength; order of wavelengths not given; Results: both sexes showed significant phototaxis across all tested wavelengths (ANOVA females F(27,56) = 6.849, p < 0.001; males F(27,56) = 13.100, p < 0.001) and full light beat darkness (p < 0.001); the Discussion says most individuals stay in the stationary zone and a small portion disperse to the light or dark zone in nearly equal numbers; per-wavelength values are only in Figure 6
quote: Phototaxis tests revealed females are highly sensitive to 360 nm, 380 nm, and 700 nm wavelengths, while males exhibit high sensitivity to 360 nm and 400 nm.
note: Sentence copied whole from the MDPI abstract (returned in two consecutive segments). Licence: page metadata CC BY 3.0, Crossref CC BY 4.0 vor. DOI, volume, issue and author order verified on Crossref. The species is on main only for opsin_sequences_recovered, not behaviour_vision.
